[4, 6] This was followed by a second October increase on October 31, 2023, which brought the minimum base price for HRC to $900 per ton. [2, 3] Subsequently, on November 7, 2023, Cleveland-Cliffs announced a further increase, setting the minimum base price for HRC at $1,000 per ton, effective immediately with all new orders. [5] These price increases also applied to the company's cold-rolled and coated steel products. [5] <2> In a report published on October 24, 2023, the World Steel Association announced that the United States produced 6.7 million tonnes (Mt) of crude steel during September 2023. This production volume represents a 2.6% increase compared to September 2022. The U.S. output was part of the 149.3 million tonnes of total crude steel produced by the 63 countries that report their data to the association. <3> Based on data from the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI), shipments from U.S. steel mills in August 2023 saw a 1.5% increase compared to the previous month. [4] However, when compared year-over-year, shipments were nearly unchanged. [4] For the year-to-date through August, total steel shipments were down 2.9% from the same eight-month period in 2022. [4] Separately, the World Steel Association reported that U.S. raw steel production in August 2023 was up 1.1% compared to August 2022, though the year-to-date production through August was down 1.9% versus the prior year. [5, 9] Capacity utilization for the week ending August 31, 2023, was reported at 76.6%, remaining below the 80% threshold. [1, 2] While demand for HRC in the United States had not fully recovered, the gradual price increases were being accepted by consumers after a prolonged period of decline earlier in the year. [1, 2] The price hikes were also supported by planned maintenance shutdowns by major U.S. steelmakers, which reduced supply. [2] <7> In early September 2023, US steel producers, distributors, and traders anticipated that steel prices for the month would either remain flat or decrease compared to August. [2] This market sentiment was primarily driven by concerns over weakening demand and the potential for strikes within the auto industry, which would further dampen steel consumption. [2, 6] <8> A September 2023 S&P Global survey revealed that US steel producers, distributors, and traders anticipated steel prices to be flat or lower compared to August. [1] This expectation was primarily driven by concerns over weakening demand and the possibility of a United Auto Workers (UAW) strike against the 'Big Three' automakers, a topic of widespread discussion in the steel market in late August. [1, 6] While the outlook for finished steel was bearish, the forecast for steel scrap was more divided; a separate Fastmarkets survey on September 1st showed over half of its respondents expected scrap prices to rise due to tight supply, while also acknowledging uncertainty due to the UAW negotiations. [8] The concerns about a strike materialized when the UAW began its industrial action on September 15, 2023, after its contract expired. [4, 11] The S&P survey's prediction proved accurate, as overall US benchmark steel prices fell by an average of 8% in September compared to August, with the strike directly impacting steel demand. [2, 5, 7] <9> Based on data from the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI), U.S. steel imports in July 2023 totaled 2.37 million tons. This figure represents a 15.2% decrease compared to June 2023. [1] For the year-to-date period of January through July 2023, steel imports saw a 10.7% decline compared to the same period in 2022. [1] <10> According to the World Steel Association (worldsteel), the United States produced 6.9 million tonnes of crude steel in July 2023, which reflects a 0.5% increase compared to July 2022. [2, 3] This was part of a total of 158.5 million tonnes produced by the 63 countries reporting to worldsteel for that month, representing a 6.6% global increase year-over-year. [1, 2]

metadata.original_text: This time series records steel CNY T data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-05-09 to 2024-05-24. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The average price of hot-rolled coil (HRC) steel in the first quarter of 2024 was influenced by market volatility, with prices experiencing a sharp rise in late 2023 and into January 2024 before declining through the end of the quarter. [2] Major producers like U.S. Steel reported capturing higher steel prices during this period, resulting in sequential increases in earnings. [11] The market dynamics were partly influenced by uncertainty and speculation surrounding potential new tariffs, which can contribute to price fluctuations. <2> On April 26, 2024, Cleveland-Cliffs announced it will start publishing a monthly "Cliffs Hot Rolled Market Price" for hot-rolled coil (HRC) in an effort to enhance market transparency, responding to industry trends and customer feedback. Lourenco Goncalves, the company's Chairman, President, and CEO, stated, "We encourage market transparency and have been pleased to see other market participants be more open with their pricing." The inaugural price was set at $850 per short ton for orders to be fulfilled in June, with the announcement coinciding with the opening of the order book. <3> During its first-quarter 2024 earnings discussion, Steel Dynamics noted a price gap between hot-rolled and cold-rolled coil that was wider than is typical. The company explained that this was due to a more constrained market for coated products. This tightness in the coated products market was, in turn, driven by significant demand from the renewable energy sector for the development of new solar projects. [1, 4] <4> The World Steel Association announced that the United States produced 6.9 million tonnes of crude steel in March 2024, a figure that remained unchanged from the production levels of March 2023. <5> On April 9, 2024, the World Steel Association (worldsteel) released its Short Range Outlook for 2024 and 2025. The forecast projects a 1.7% rebound in global steel demand for 2024, reaching 1,793 million tonnes. For developed economies, a strengthening recovery of 1.3% is expected in 2024, with the United States' demand noted as continuing to show healthy fundamentals and being expected to return to a growth path. The outlook also anticipates further global growth of 1.2% in 2025. <6> Nucor Corporation announced on April 4, 2024, that it was introducing a new pricing mechanism, the weekly Consumer Spot Price (CSP), for hot-rolled coil (HRC). [1, 2, 9] The first CSP was issued on Monday, April 8, 2024. [1, 3, 6] This initiative was designed to increase transparency and provide customers with consistent, timely information to help them make business decisions, reduce their reliance on market speculation, and manage risk. [1, 2, 6] According to the announcement, the CSP is released every Monday, is derived from both quantitative and qualitative data, and applies to spot orders with lead times of three to five weeks. [2, 3] <7> United States Steel Corp. announced on March 18, 2024, its earnings guidance for the first fiscal quarter of 2024. The company projected an adjusted earnings per diluted share (EPS) to be in the range of $0.80 to $0.84. This forecast was below the analyst consensus expectation of $0.89 per share. Alongside the EPS guidance, U.S. Steel also anticipated its first-quarter adjusted EBITDA to be approximately $425 million, which was also below the consensus estimate of $467.5 million. The company's President and CEO, David B. Burritt, stated that the anticipated performance was in line with their prior outlook, citing healthy steel demand and strong operating performance as key factors. The actual results for the quarter, reported on May 2, 2024, were an adjusted net earnings of $0.82 per diluted share, falling within the guided range. <8> A weekly market report for the week ending March 15, 2024, indicated a significant decline in West Coast USA steel scrap prices. The largest decrease was seen in Shredded Auto Scrap, with prices falling by 11.24% compared to the prior week. Additionally, #1 Bundle prices dropped by 10%, #1 Busheling prices fell by 9.57%, and Sheet Metal prices decreased by 7.41%. <9> Citing data from the US Department of Commerce, U.S. steel exports saw a significant rebound in January, increasing by 25% to 770,649 short tons. This jump followed a 12-month low recorded in the previous month, December.

[11] This statement was made in the context of a challenging quarter with lower-than-expected realized pricing and a generally weak demand environment. [6, 11] The commentary followed a significant drop in US hot-rolled coil (HRC) prices, which had fallen from over $1,100 per short ton early in 2024 to approximately $670 per short ton in late June and $650 per short ton by the end of July. This decline is part of a broader trend, with U.S. steel production for the first half of 2024, from January to June, totaling 40.0 million tonnes, a 2.4% decrease compared to the same period in 2023. This data indicates a sustained year-over-year reduction in domestic steel output. <4> On July 10, 2024, the White House announced measures to counter the circumvention of Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs by China through Mexico. Effective immediately, a new regulation requires that steel products from Mexico must be 'melted and poured' in North America (United States, Mexico, or Canada) to qualify for tariff exemptions. Steel articles and derivative products from Mexico that do not meet this requirement are subject to a 25% tariff. This action is intended to close a loophole that allowed Chinese steel to be processed in Mexico and then enter the U.S. market duty-free under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). This decline was largely attributed to cautious buying behavior, as market participants waited for prices to bottom out due to an imbalance of supply and demand. Reports from early in the month indicated that while mechanical tubing prices remained flat, structural tubing prices had started to decrease. By late June, weak demand for Hot-Rolled Coil (HRC) sheet continued to exert downward pressure on prices, with American steelmaker Nucor announcing a reduction in its weekly HRC prices to stimulate sales. The influx of steel imports was also cited as a factor straining domestic prices. This overall market softness and price decline for certain steel products occurred throughout the month. <8> Major U.S. steel producers, including U.S. Steel, Nucor, and Steel Dynamics, issued lower profit guidance for the second quarter of 2024, primarily attributing the reduced expectations to declining steel prices. [4, 8] Nucor anticipated second-quarter earnings to fall to $2.20-$2.30 per diluted share from $3.46 in the first quarter. [4] Similarly, U.S. Steel expected adjusted net earnings of $0.76-$0.80 per diluted share, a decrease from $0.82 in the first quarter. [4] Steel Dynamics also projected that its second-quarter profitability would be "meaningfully lower" than the previous quarter, citing lower realized pricing as the key factor. [4, 8] <9> In response to a slowdown in market demand, American steelmaker Nucor announced multiple weekly reductions in its Hot-Rolled Coil (HRC) prices during June 2024. [7] On June 17, Nucor reduced its consumer spot price (CSP) by $5 per short ton to $715, which followed a more significant $60 per ton cut the previous week. [2] The company announced a further and more substantial price drop on June 24, reducing the weekly HRC price by $35 per short ton to $680. [1] By the beginning of June, Nucor's CSP had already fallen by $100 per ton from its price at the start of the month. [1] The broader U.S. HRC market saw prices continue to drift lower throughout the month due to weak demand and pressure from imports, forcing domestic mills to lower prices to secure orders. [3, 5, 7] <10> The American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI) reported that domestic steel mill shipments; domestic steel mill shipments in April 2023 were 7,499,979 short tons

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Nucor announced a $30 per ton ($1.50 per hundredweight) increase in its domestic wire rod pricing, which went into effect on December 11, 2025. <2> On February 12, 2026, steelmakers Gerdau and Steel Dynamics Inc. announced a price increase of $40 to $60 per ton on their posted prices for wide flange beams, standard beams, miscellaneous beams, piling, and select angles and channels. <3> Nucor increased its Consumer Spot Price (CSP) for hot-rolled coil to $975 per short ton for most of its mills, and raised the CSP for its West Coast joint venture, California Steel Industries (CSI), to $1,025 per short ton. <4> The US domestic ferrous scrap market largely settled its February pricing with a general increase of $20 to $30 per gross ton compared to January. The price jump was significantly driven by severe winter storms sweeping across the eastern half of the country, which stalled logistics, slowed scrap flows into processors' yards, and tightened overall supply. <5> Steel Dynamics reported its fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 financial results, revealing that the average external selling price for its steel operations decreased to $1,089 per ton for the year. The company also noted a sequential decline in Q4 average realized flat-rolled steel pricing, attributing the drop to commercial contracts priced on a lagging indexed basis. <6> On January 9, 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce announced a preliminary affirmative determination to impose countervailing duties of 29.51% on steel concrete reinforcing bar (rebar) imports from Egypt. These provisional duties, effective January 13, 2026, were implemented to counteract government subsidies received by Egyptian producers and exporters that unfairly impacted U.S. market pricing. <7> On January 12, 2026, reports confirmed that Nucor Corporation maintained its hot-rolled coil (HRC) spot price at $950 per ton for the fourth consecutive week. This deliberate price hold is intended to test the market's price elasticity by gauging resistance from service centers and OEMs without immediately implementing discounts. <8> Morgan Stanley upgraded Cleveland-Cliffs stock from 'Equal Weight' to 'Overweight' and established a $17.00 price target. The firm noted that the protectionist environment, characterized by firm 50% steel tariffs, is expected to maintain a high pricing floor and keep steel prices elevated. <9> Commercial Metals Company (CMC) reported its fiscal first-quarter 2026 financial results for the period ended November 30, 2025. The company highlighted that robust domestic market conditions, characterized by stable demand, led to its North America Steel Group's metal margins expanding sequentially by $53 per ton. This margin expansion was primarily fueled by a $57 per ton improvement in the average selling price of its steel products alongside stable scrap costs.
